description: REX-Ray is a container storage orchestration engine enabling persistence for cloud native workloads

summary.one_liner: REX-Ray is a vendor-agnostic storage orchestration engine that provides persistent storage volumes for Docker, Kubernetes, and Mesos workloads across many cloud and storage platforms.
summary.what_it_does: REX-Ray runs as a standalone process, a client-server model, a Go package, a CLI tool, or a Linux service. The CLI lists and manages volumes (for example, `rexray volume ls`). The service mode exposes an HTTP/JSON interface so Docker, Mesos, and similar platforms can request volume attachment, discovery, formatting, and mounting. It also installs as a Docker plugin (Docker 1.13+) so containers can use a volume driver directly. The README lists supported providers including Amazon EBS/EFS/S3FS, Ceph RBD, Dell EMC Isilon and ScaleIO, DigitalOcean Block Storage, Google Persistent Disk, Microsoft Azure Unmanaged Disk, OpenStack Cinder, and VirtualBox. Supported operating systems include Ubuntu, Debian, RedHat, CentOS, CoreOS, and OS X, with Windows not supported. The README also states that CSI support is planned once CSI reaches version 1.0.
use_cases: attach cloud block volumes to kubernetes or mesos workloads
manage ebs volumes from the command line
mount openstack cinder or google persistent disk into containers
use ceph rbd or dell emc storage as docker volumes
how_to_run: curl -sSL | sh -  (install script, URL omitted in README)
export REXRAY_SERVICE=ebs; export EBS_ACCESSKEY=...; export EBS_SECRETKEY=...
docker plugin install rexray/ebs EBS_ACCESSKEY=access_key EBS_SECRETKEY=secret_key
notable: Vendor-agnostic storage orchestration with many cloud and on-prem storage backends behind one interface
Runs as CLI, background service, or Docker managed plugin
Client-server architecture where the client handles local device attach, format, and mount
Go package usable as a library
caveats: Windows is not supported; the OS support table lists no Windows entries
CSI support is deferred until CSI 1.0, which the README projects for late 2018
Hosted unstable and staged binaries older than 0.11.2-rc1 were pruned, so older builds may be unavailable
Provider setup requires cloud credentials and per-provider configuration, documented externally
